items.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: me and Tootie Heath. We replaced Flanagan and uh Elvin.

ctx.x: When, when you, you say, he noticed you at a jam session at Birdland …
Uh-hm. That's what he told me and uh next thing I knew I was in his band, me and Tootie Heath. We replaced Flanagan and uh Elvin.
You know, what was, was there a given circle of musicians that were at Birdland during those sessions?

items.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Me and Albert Heath uh both uh moved over to the Jazztet

ctx.x: Now the next move is Jazztet. How did you get to the Jazztet? Wht were the circumstances that led you to that?

Uh, a ten dollar raise. You know, back in those days that ten dollars was that important. [chuckles] So … Me and Albert Heath uh both uh moved over to the Jazztet, replacing uh McCoy Tyner and uh, uh, oh, let me see, who was it? Might have been on drums. Oh, Lex Humphries is the guy that had been on drums, yeah, so …. It was a long time ago but I remember those moves at least, and it was uh, the difference uh …
Was Curtis there when you got there? Or was it Tom …
